app.title: DBREF-SIFTS
app.summary: A person enters one or more PDB entry IDs and chooses whether to take the curated SIFTS mapping or derive one automatically by searching the source organism's proteome and aligning each chain against the candidates. Settings decide the identity threshold for automatic matches, whether only reviewed Swiss-Prot entries count, whether adjacent segments are merged, and whether records come out in fixed wwPDB columns or tab-delimited. For each entry the tool shows the DBREF records that map chain residue ranges to UniProt ranges, a details table with identity, coverage and review status, and notes on unmatched or hidden chains. The person downloads the records per entry, or for all entries as one file.

task.text: Produce DBREF cross-reference records that map each protein chain of a structure entry to its UniProtKB sequence ranges, using either curated or sequence-derived mappings.

data.text: Protein structure entries fetched from the PDBe API, with their chain sequences and residue numbering, matched against UniProtKB sequences and metadata.
data.item: a segment: a stretch of residues in one chain of a structure entry, aligned to a range in one UniProt sequence

stage.text: cross-referencing structure chains to sequence databases when annotating a structure entry

mechanism.text: Sidebar settings choose the mapping method and output options, and a text box of entry IDs drives the main page, which shows a block of records, a download button and an expandable details table for each entry. When several entries are entered, a combined download sits above them all.

field.text: structure-to-sequence residue mapping in structural bioinformatics

workflow.name: map items to reference records and export them in a standard format

steps.step: choose how the matches are made
steps.here: Radio picks Curated (SIFTS) or Automated (PDBe-SIFTS). A minimum-identity slider (50–100%, default 90%) is only enabled under Automated, and a Swiss-Prot-only box limits matches to reviewed entries.
Type one or more four-character PDB IDs separated by spaces or commas. Invalid IDs stop the run with an error.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: For each entry, either read the SIFTS segments, or scan the organism's UniProt proteome for the exact chain sequence, then run a Smith-Waterman alignment (BLOSUM62) and accept the hit only above the identity threshold and 50% coverage. Positions are then translated to author residue numbering.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Unreviewed (TrEMBL) hits are hidden when Swiss-Prot only is on, and segments that continue across a gap can be merged into one record.

The Mapping details expander lists each segment's chain, entity, source, PDB and UniProt ranges, identity, coverage, review status, protein and organism, with notes on unmatched entities or missing numbering.
Records are shown in fixed wwPDB columns or tab-delimited form. They download as a .txt or .tsv file per entry, or as one combined file for all entries.

distinctive: Records follow the legacy wwPDB v3.3 DBREF column layout, and fields widen instead of truncating when modern accessions do not fit
Two sources can be swapped, curated SIFTS or sequence-derived, so the automatic one also works as a check on the curated mapping
Alignment positions are translated to author residue numbering with insertion codes, and unobserved residues are extrapolated from the nearest observed one
Automatic matches must pass both an identity threshold and a minimum chain coverage, and the reason for each rejection is reported
